submission.rationale: The planning-time intent was to checkpoint beta as complete only if the newer Task state still supports that semantic transition. The consequence boundary evidence shows the revision advanced 3→4 and the checkpoint digest changed (sha256 differs), even though frontier/nextActions appear unchanged and only an "established evidence statement" was appended. Because the owner action contract requires the checkpoint to match expectedRevision and the semantic applicability (beta→beta-complete) can only be verified by reobserving the actual Task state, I cannot safely commit a rebase or act unbound without a reobservation. The digest change is a meaningful delta that could affect the semantic transition, so REOBSERVE_THEN_DECIDE is the correct posture — do not force a consequence that may conflict.
